title: Sense IC must be placed adjacent to its shunt inner edge
rule: Every primary sense IC (INA228/INA238/INA240) must be placed with its sense-input pads (IN+/IN− or HI/LO) within 3 mm of the corresponding shunt resistor's inner Kelvin-sense edge. The IC may not be separated from its shunt by another component, a pour boundary crossing, or a via field.
scope: Every (RS*, U*) pair where U* is an INA228/INA238/INA240 and RS* is its assigned shunt — derivable from the netlist: U.IN+ net == RS._HI net AND U.IN− net == RS._LO net
rationale: Kelvin four-wire sensing requires the shortest possible sense path between the shunt inner edge and the IC differential inputs to minimise IR drop and pickup in the sense loop. §6.8 locks this as a layout requirement.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8: 'Keep the Kelvin sense pair short and local on the top layer next to the shunt and its monitor.'
check_method: For each (shunt_ref, ic_ref) Kelvin pair derived from net topology, compute distance from ic_ref sense-pad centroid to shunt_ref inner-edge pad centroid; fail if > 3 mm.
existing_checker: chk_kelvin_topology in cec_synth_pipeline.py (verifies shunt straddles HI/LO + INA on it); cec_score.py kelvin_ok gate (routing completeness)

title: Kelvin sense traces must stay on L1/F.Cu with no vias
rule: All traces on the *_HI/*_LO Kelvin sense nets (and IN*_P/IN*_N on 12VHPWR) must be routed entirely on the top copper layer (F.Cu / Layer 0). No via may appear on these nets between the shunt inner-edge pad and the IC differential input pin. Routing to an inner layer and back is prohibited.
scope: All nets matching *_HI, *_LO, IN*_P, IN*_N that connect a shunt pad to an INA input pin — derivable from netlist net names
rationale: §6.8 explicitly prohibits routing Kelvin sense down to a signal layer and back. A via adds barrel resistance and inductance to the sense loop, corrupting the differential measurement.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8: 'Do not route it down to a signal layer and back.'
check_method: Parse routed .kicad_pcb: for each track segment on a *_HI/*_LO/IN*_P/IN*_N net, assert layer == F.Cu (layer index 0). Assert no PCB_VIA exists on these nets.
existing_checker: cec_score.py kelvin_ok gate (routing completeness); no layer-specific check yet — gap

title: Kelvin sense pair traces must be length-matched
rule: Within each Kelvin pair (*_HI/*_LO or IN*_P/IN*_N), the routed trace lengths from the shunt inner-edge pads to the IC differential input pads must match within 0.5 mm. Asymmetric lengths create a skew-resistance imbalance in the sense loop.
scope: Each (*_HI, *_LO) or (IN*_P, IN*_N) net pair connected between a shunt and its INA — same derivation as kelvin-sense-adjacent-shunt
rationale: Even at near-DC, a mismatched Kelvin stub adds a net series resistance to one arm, producing a systematic offset proportional to the current carried by the sense trace (parasitic current in the sense loop from board leakage/ground offsets).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8 (Kelvin four-wire geometry); CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR note: 'length-match the straight run in the GUI if the inner/outer spread matters'
check_method: Compute routed trace length for each net in the pair (sum of segment lengths from shunt pad to IC pin); assert |len_HI − len_LO| ≤ 0.5 mm.

title: EPS and PCIe per-cable shunt must be 0.5 mΩ
rule: Every shunt resistor on an EPS 8-pin or PCIe 8-pin module (refs RS1, RS2 on EPS; RS1–RS3 on PCIe-3port) must have a BOM value of 0.5 mΩ (0.0005 Ω). Any other value is a spec violation per §6.4.
scope: All refs matching RS* on boards eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port
rationale: §6.4 shunt table locked. 0.5 mΩ is sized for the ~40–55 A per-cable EPS/PCIe current class: sufficient voltage across the shunt for the INA238 to resolve, while minimising I²R drop and heat at full load.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: 'EPS and PCIe per-cable = 0.5 mΩ'
check_method: Parse BOM/schematic Value field for RS* on EPS/PCIe boards; assert Value == '0.5mΩ' or '0.0005' (normalised). Implemented in chk_shunt_values() of cec_synth_pipeline.py.

title: 12VHPWR per-pin shunt must be 1 mΩ
rule: Every per-pin shunt on the 12VHPWR Standard or Pro module (refs RS1–RS6) must have a BOM value of 1 mΩ (0.001 Ω) per §6.4.
scope: All refs matching RS* on boards 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro
rationale: §6.4 locked. 1 mΩ is sized for the ~9.2 A/pin 12V-2x6 class with INA240 gain-20 amplification giving sufficient ADC headroom.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: '12VHPWR per-pin = 1 mΩ'
check_method: Parse BOM Value for RS* on 12vhpwr-* boards; assert Value == '1mΩ' or '0.001'.

title: 24-pin ATX main rail shunts 2 mΩ; 5VSB shunt 25 mΩ
rule: On the atx-24pin module: RS1 (12V), RS2 (5V), RS3 (3.3V) must each be 2 mΩ. RS4 (5VSB) must be 25 mΩ. Any other value violates §6.4.
scope: Refs RS1–RS4 on board atx-24pin; identifiable by net: RS4 straddles the 5VSB_HI/5VSB_LO net pair
rationale: §6.4 locked. 5VSB carries much lower current (<3 A) so a higher shunt value gives better LSB resolution with the INA228's 195 µV bus LSB.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: '24-pin 12V/5V/3V3 = 2 mΩ, 24-pin 5VSB = 25 mΩ'
check_method: Parse BOM; RS1–RS3 assert 0.002 Ω; RS4 assert 0.025 Ω. Net connectivity distinguishes RS4 (its HI net contains '5VSB').
existing_checker: chk_shunt_values in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage NOTE (merged dup): chk_shunt_values currently uses a single want_ohms=0.5mOhm default -- needs per-board values to enforce the 2mOhm/25mOhm 24-pin table.

title: Shunt footprint must expose all four Kelvin pads
rule: Every shunt resistor must use a footprint that exposes distinct force pads (F+, F−) and sense pads (S+, S−) as separate copper lands. The footprint must NOT merge sense into the force pad (i.e. a plain 2-pad R_2512 is acceptable only when Kelvin taps are drawn in copper on the outer pad edges; a WSK2512 4-terminal is preferred but the 2-pad R_2512 with Kelvin annotation is the generator default). Either way, the BOM part must be a metal-element low-TCR shunt with sense terminals accessible.
scope: All RS* shunt footprints on every module board
rationale: §6.8 four-wire Kelvin sensing. A standard 2-terminal resistor footprint with sense tapped off the solder pad is acceptable only if the Kelvin tap is drawn at the inner pad edge (not the same via as the force current). The generator currently uses R_2512 with external Kelvin copper — §6.8 documents this choice.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8; CLAUDE.md: 'Shunt land = honest 2-pad R_2512 (Kelvin taps drawn in copper at layout, §6.8) — NOT the 4-terminal WSK2512'
check_method: Check footprint name for RS* refs: must be R_2512, CSS2H-2512R, WSK2512, or another 2512-class metal-element land. Flag any 0402/0603/0805 footprint on RS*.

title: J_IN → shunt → J_OUT corridor must be a routing keepout
rule: On every cable-interposer module (EPS, PCIe), the rectangular corridor from J_IN power pins through each shunt RS* to the corresponding J_OUT power pins must be reserved as a routing keepout for all copper except the high-current 12V and GND pours that belong to that corridor. No signal trace, via, or foreign net copper may enter the corridor. The keepout region per cable is defined by the bounding box of J_IN power pads + shunt pads + J_OUT power pads, expanded by 0.5 mm on each side. No logic ICs or non-shunt components may sit in the power lane (the placement half of this rule). (merged dup)
scope: Each cable column on EPS (2 cables) and PCIe (2 or 3 cables); derivable from J_IN*/J_OUT* footprint positions and RS* positions in .kicad_pcb
rationale: CLAUDE.md action item -2 explicitly names 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as the first required addition to the domain-blind placer. Foreign copper in the corridor creates unexpected current return paths and heating.
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation'; §6.7: 'high-current pour corridor (J_IN->shunt->J_OUT) kept clear'
check_method: For each cable's corridor bbox, query all copper objects (tracks, vias, zone fills) that intersect the bbox; assert all belong to the corridor's *_HI or GND nets only.
existing_checker: cec_fr.bake_hints() emits keep-out rule areas into the DSN for Freerouting; no post-route checker yet

title: 12V and GND high-current paths must use copper pours, not fat traces
rule: The +12V and GND high-current nets on every module board must be realized as filled copper zone pours (ZONE_FILLER). Fat single traces are prohibited for these nets on the outer layers. Minimum pour area per cable: ≥ 100 mm² on each outer layer (F.Cu and B.Cu) in the corridor, achieving ≥ 200 mm² total cross-section per cable at 2oz copper.
scope: Nets *_HI (SENSEC*_HI, SENSEP*_HI) and GND on EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards; +12V net on 12VHPWR
rationale: CLAUDE.md routing notes: 'current is carried by copper AREA'; cec_router Done section: 'a 2.5mm trace won't fit channels FR routed at 0.2mm — post-hoc widening COLLIDES; current is carried by copper AREA. So GND (already a plane), the 12V SENSEC nets belong as FILLED POURS'. Freerouting ignores netclass widths, so pours are the only reliable path.
source: CLAUDE.md Done (route-to-clean): 'HIGH-CURRENT = POURS, NOT FAT TRACES'; §6.7: 'size each path's via array for full current'
check_method: Parse .kicad_pcb: for each high-current net, assert at least one filled_polygon zone exists on F.Cu and B.Cu in the corridor; assert no single track segment on these nets has width < 1.0 mm (i.e. thin traces are only acceptable as Kelvin sense stubs, which are on the sense nets not the force nets).
existing_checker: cec_fr.add_power_pours() / derive_power_pours() add pours post-route; no area-floor checker

title: Outer copper layers must be 2 oz for high-current modules
rule: The PCB stackup for all cable-interposer modules (EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR) must specify 2 oz (70 µm) copper on both outer layers (F.Cu, B.Cu) and 1 oz (35 µm) on both inner layers. The .kicad_pcb stackup section must reflect this. A 1oz outer layer fails the IPC-2221 temperature gate at full cable current.
scope: All cable-interposer module boards: eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port, 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro
rationale: §6.7 and CLAUDE.md: '4-layer, 2oz outer / 1oz inner'. The electrothermal model in cec_synth_pipeline.electrothermal_solve() uses CU_OZ_MM = 0.0348 per oz; the physics gate flags a conductor-over-temp (dT > 30°C) condition that only passes at 2oz outer.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7; CLAUDE.md: '4-layer 2oz outer / 1oz inner (hpwr: 12V on both outers, GND both inners; cable boards In1=GND, In2=12V)'
check_method: Parse .kicad_pcb stackup copper_finish / dielectric entries; assert F.Cu and B.Cu thickness ≥ 0.070 mm (2oz); assert In1.Cu and In2.Cu thickness ≈ 0.035 mm (1oz).
existing_checker: electrothermal_solve in cec_synth_pipeline.py uses CU_OZ_MM constant but does not parse stackup from board file — gap

title: Via fields at shunt terminals and connector pins must carry full current
rule: Each shunt terminal pad and each high-current connector pin (J_IN/J_OUT power pins) must have a via field of at least 5 vias (drill ≥ 0.5 mm, pad ≥ 0.9 mm) connecting F.Cu to B.Cu, uniformly spaced within the pad or the surrounding copper pour. For the EPS/PCIe ~40–55 A class, a field of ≥ 6 vias per shunt terminal is required to avoid the via-over-temp physics gate.
scope: All RS* shunt terminal pads and J_IN*/J_OUT* power pads on EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards; derivable from pad net membership in *_HI or GND
rationale: §6.7: 'size each path's via array for full current.' CLAUDE.md: 'stitch F<->B ~5mm down each lane + a field of 5-6 per shunt terminal + 3-6 per J3/J4 power pin'. The electrothermal model (physics_gates()) fires via-over-temp when the via array is undersized.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7; CLAUDE.md routing plan: 'current-carrying vias 0.5mm drill / 0.9mm pad (~2A @10C), stitch F<->B ~5mm down each lane + a field of 5-6 per shunt terminal'
check_method: For each RS* shunt pad and each J_IN/J_OUT power pad, count PCB_VIA objects within 2 mm of the pad centroid on the same net; assert count ≥ 5 (EPS/PCIe) or ≥ 3 (12VHPWR per-pin).
existing_checker: physics_gates() in cec_synth_pipeline.py checks via-over-temp via barrel cross-section; no explicit count check

title: EPS/PCIe shunts require TIM pad and bare PCB contact land for chassis coupling
rule: On EPS and PCIe modules, each shunt RS* must have a clear B.Cu area (no solder mask, no silk, no via drill-out) on the underside beneath the shunt body, sized for a thermal interface material (TIM) pad to couple heat to the chassis. The B.Cu area must be at least as large as the shunt body (≥ 6.3 mm × 3.2 mm for R_2512) and must be on GND or the pour net (no isolated copper island).
scope: All RS* refs on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port
rationale: §6.6: 'chassis thermal coupling / TIM under the EPS/PCIe shunts'. At 40–55 A the shunt dissipates up to ~1.2 W per element; chassis coupling is required to keep junction temperature within bounds without an active heatsink.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.6 (v3.10 addition): 'chassis thermal coupling / TIM under the EPS/PCIe shunts'
check_method: Check for a B.Cu copper zone or courtyard annotation under each RS* at ≥ 6.3×3.2 mm; check no solder mask opening is missing (B.Mask should be cleared). Partial check via courtyard geometry.

title: INA181 transient-detection amp must have its own independent Kelvin pair on the shunt
rule: Per §6.13: the INA181A2 taps the same shunt as the INA238 but with its OWN dedicated Kelvin sense pair. The INA238's _HI/_LO sense traces and the INA181's input traces must be electrically independent copper paths from the shunt inner edges — they may share the same net node (the shunt force net) only at the shunt pad itself, not via a shared trace. One INA181 per cable; muxing across cables is prohibited.
scope: Each (RS*, U_INA238*, U_INA181*) triplet per cable on EPS/PCIe boards — derivable from schematic: the INA181 IN+ and IN− nets must connect directly to the shunt pads, not to the INA238 input pads
rationale: §6.13: 'An INA181A2 (gain 50) tapping the same shunt as the INA238 with its own Kelvin pair... One comparator per cable, since muxing would miss spikes on the unwatched channel.' A shared sense trace adds the INA238 input network's impedance to the INA181's signal path, corrupting transient detection.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.13
check_method: Netlist check: for each INA181 U20*/U21*/U22*, assert its IN+ net connects directly to the RS* shunt force pad (no intermediate pad belonging to INA238). Assert no net is shared between INA238.IN+ and INA181.IN+ for the same cable.

title: INA181 transient-detection IC must be adjacent to its shunt
rule: Each INA181A2 (refs U20*, U21*, U22* on EPS/PCIe) must be placed with its input pads (IN+/IN−) within 3 mm of the corresponding shunt RS* inner Kelvin-sense edge, on the same side of the board (F.Cu side). Same proximity rule as the primary INA238.
scope: All U20*/U21*/U22* INA181 refs on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port — derivable from Value field containing 'INA181'
rationale: §6.13 specifies the INA181 taps the shunt with its own Kelvin pair; a remote placement introduces trace inductance in the sense path, degrading the fast-transient response the INA181 is specifically chosen for (bandwidth >> INA238).
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.13; CLAUDE.md action item -2: 'sense devices (INA238/INA181) sit hard against their shunt's inner edge'
check_method: Same distance check as kelvin-sense-adjacent-shunt but applied to INA181 refs: centroid of INA181 IN+/IN− pads ≤ 3 mm from RS* inner pad centroid.

title: One INA181 + one TLV7011 comparator per cable; no shared/muxed detection
rule: Each cable on an EPS or PCIe module must have exactly one INA181A2 and one TLV7011 comparator dedicated to it. Sharing one INA181 or comparator across two cables (via analog mux or otherwise) is prohibited. The count of INA181 refs must equal the number of cables (2 for EPS/PCIe-2port, 3 for PCIe-3port). Same for TLV7011.
scope: Refs U20*, U21*, U22* (INA181) and U30*, U31*, U32* (TLV7011) on EPS/PCIe boards; count verified against board cable count N in gen-modules.py
rationale: §6.13: 'One comparator per cable, since muxing would miss spikes on the unwatched channel.' Transient detection is time-critical; a muxed path introduces dead-time during which a transient on the unmonitored cable goes undetected.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.13
check_method: Count refs with Value='INA181A2IDBVR' and Value='TLV7011DBVR' in BOM; assert each count == N_cables (2 or 3).
existing_checker: chk_kelvin_topology in cec_synth_pipeline.py (partial — checks INA presence but not INA181 count)

title: THRESH PWM reference shared across all comparators on the same board
rule: All TLV7011 comparator threshold inputs (non-inverting reference input) on a board must connect to the single shared THRESH net driven by one MCU PWM pin (IO14) through one R/C low-pass filter (R10 10kΩ + C40 100nF). Multiple independent THRESH nets or multiple R/C filters driving separate comparator references are prohibited.
scope: THRESH net and all TLV7011 non-inverting inputs on EPS/PCIe boards; derivable from netlist: all V+ pins of TLV7011 instances must connect to the same THRESH net node
rationale: §6.13 firmware-settable threshold: a single firmware-controlled PWM reference simplifies calibration and ensures a consistent detection threshold across all cables. Independent thresholds per cable would require N PWM channels and complicate firmware.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.13: 'firmware-settable threshold -> ORs into the §6.10 FREEZE trigger'
check_method: Netlist: for each TLV7011 ref, assert its non-inverting input pin connects to the net named THRESH (or THRESH_PWM). Assert exactly one MCU pin connects to THRESH.

title: TLV7011 comparator output must connect to a dedicated MCU GPIO that ORs into FREEZE
rule: Each TLV7011's open-drain output must connect to a distinct MCU GPIO pin (DET_CABLE1, DET_CABLE2, DET_CABLE3) with a pull-up resistor. The MCU firmware treats any asserted DET_* as a FREEZE trigger. The DET nets must not be shared or wire-OR'd in hardware; each cable's detection event must be independently readable by firmware.
scope: DET_CABLE* nets and TLV7011 output pins on EPS/PCIe boards; MCU GPIO assignments derivable from CLAUDE.md action item -1 netlist verification
rationale: §6.13: 'flags a transient as a BINARY event... ORs into the §6.10 FREEZE trigger'. Independent per-cable GPIO enables firmware to identify which cable triggered, not just that a trigger occurred.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.13; CLAUDE.md action item -1: '§6.13 chain... per-cable DET -> MCU GPIO latch, ORs into FREEZE'
check_method: Netlist: for each TLV7011, assert its output net connects to exactly one MCU GPIO pad (pad on ESP32-C6-MINI-1) and to a pull-up resistor going to +3V3. Assert no two TLV7011 outputs share a net.

title: PSU-side power connectors must face outward to their designated board edge
rule: J_IN (PSU-side) power connectors must be placed at the top board edge with the connector mouth facing upward (+y direction out) and rotated 180°. J_OUT (load-side) connectors must be at the bottom edge with mouth facing downward (−y direction out) and rotated 0°. For 12VHPWR, J3 is at top (rot 180, mouth −y per the Molex 219116 native mouth-on-+y geometry) and J4 at bottom (rot 0). This orientation ensures the PSU cable seats without the PCB fouling the plug overmold.
scope: All J_IN* and J_OUT* refs on EPS/PCIe; J3/J4 on 12vhpwr-standard/pro; derivable from ref prefix J_IN/J_OUT and footprint mouth-direction convention
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'J_IN rot180 / J_OUT rot0 (87427 is mirrored)'; '12VHPWR: mouth-out-the-edge needs J3 rot 180 / J4 rot 0'. Incorrect orientation means the cable cannot be plugged in without extreme force or cannot be plugged in at all.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'J_IN rot180 / J_OUT rot0'; Molex 219116 note: 'its mouth is on +y, so mouth-out-the-edge needs J3 rot 180 / J4 rot 0'
check_method: Parse .kicad_pcb: for refs J_IN*, assert rotation == 180 and Y position within 2 mm of top board edge. For J_OUT*, assert rotation == 0 and Y position within 2 mm of bottom board edge. For 12VHPWR J3: rot == 180; J4: rot == 0.
existing_checker: seed_anchors() in cec_synth_pipeline.py places power_in → top, power_out → bottom

title: 12VHPWR per-pin lane lengths must be symmetric (< 1 mm delta)
rule: On 12VHPWR Standard and Pro modules, the six per-pin current-sense lanes (J3 pin N → RS_N shunt → J4 pin N) must have equal high-current path lengths within ±1 mm. The fan-out geometry from the 3mm-pitch connector to the 6mm-pitch INA240 sense columns must be symmetric left–right.
scope: 12VHPWR per-pin lanes on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro; derivable from J3/J4 footprint pin positions and RS1–RS6 positions
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'Symmetric fan = equal-length lane pairs (length-match the straight run in the GUI if the inner/outer spread matters; the 1mΩ shunt + contact R dominate).' Asymmetric lanes create per-pin current measurement offsets due to differential I·R drop along the force path.
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR routing plan: 'Symmetric fan = equal-length lane pairs'
check_method: For each pair of symmetric lanes (inner pair lanes 3&4, middle pair 2&5, outer pair 1&6), compute the routed length of the high-current net from J3 pad to RS shunt pad; assert |len_inner_left − len_inner_right| ≤ 1 mm per pair.

title: NTC TH1 must be placed at J3 +12V pins; TH2 at cool ambient edge
rule: On 12VHPWR Standard: TH1 (shunt/board temperature NTC) must be placed within 5 mm of the J3 connector +12V pins (the row adjacent to the signal pins, per the CEM5.1 assignment). TH2 (ambient NTC) must be placed at the opposite board edge from J3, away from the high-current corridor, to measure ambient temperature for dT correction.
scope: Refs TH1, TH2 on 12vhpwr-standard; TH1 net TEMP1 → IO13, TH2 net TEMP2 → IO14
rationale: §6.1 v3.7: 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient'. The dT-above-ambient figure used for INA240 gain/shunt-TCR correction requires TH2 to be thermally isolated from the shunt. If TH1 is far from the shunt, it reads a cooler temperature and underestimates TCR correction.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1 (v3.7 addition); CLAUDE.md: 'TH1 at the J3 +12V pins, TH2 ambient, into spare ADC2 IO13/IO14'
check_method: Assert TH1 centroid distance to nearest J3 power pad ≤ 5 mm. Assert TH2 centroid distance from J3 connector centroid ≥ 20 mm (board length dependent but must be at opposite side).

title: Sense ICs must be outside the high-current pour zone with ≥ 3 mm gap
rule: No INA228/INA238/INA240/INA181 body or pad may be located inside the high-current copper pour zone (the J_IN→shunt→J_OUT corridor). The IC's courtyard must be separated from the pour boundary by ≥ 3 mm. This prevents the IC die temperature from being elevated by pour-conducted heat, which would corrupt the sense measurement via amplifier offset drift.
scope: All INA* refs on cable-interposer boards; pour zone defined as the high-current corridor keepout rectangle
rationale: CLAUDE.md action item -2: 'thermal separation' listed as a required constraint for the resumed placer design pass. Sense ICs adjacent to a pour carrying 40 A will see elevated ambient temperature.
source: CLAUDE.md action item -2: '(3) the rest of the considerations list (thermal sep...)'; §6.6 thermal coupling section
check_method: For each INA* ref, compute minimum distance from its courtyard bbox to the high-current pour zone polygon; assert ≥ 3 mm.

title: INA240 input anti-alias RC filter must be matched 10 Ω + 470 nF, fc ≈ 16.9 kHz
rule: Each INA240 differential input channel must have a matched pair of series resistors RFH*/RFL* (10 Ω, 0.1%, 50 ppm, 0402) and a differential capacitor CF* (470 nF) forming a first-order filter with fc = 1/(2π × 2×10 × 470n) ≈ 16.9 kHz. The 10 Ω value must not exceed TI's INA240 input ceiling for CMRR/gain error.
scope: All RFH*/RFL* (series input) and CF* (diff cap) refs on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro; derivable from ref naming convention in gen-modules.py
rationale: §6.1 v3.4: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470 nF differential cap (CF1-6), fc ≈ 16.9 kHz so the ~10 kHz GPU transients pass at ~−1.3 dB and HF rolls off ahead of the ADC; Rf held at 10 ohm + matched (TI's INA240 ceiling) for negligible gain/CMRR error.'
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1 v3.4; CLAUDE.md: 'matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input + 470nF differential cap'
check_method: BOM check: RFH*/RFL* Value == '10R' and Tolerance == '0.1%'; CF* Value == '470nF'. Count: must be 12 RFH/RFL (6 pairs) and 6 CF on 12VHPWR-Standard.

title: RC anti-alias filter must be placed at the INA240 end, not the shunt end
rule: The RFH*/RFL* series resistors and CF* capacitor for each INA240 channel must be placed within 3 mm of the INA240's IN+/IN− pads (the IC end), not at the shunt. The filter components serve as ADC input protection and anti-alias, which requires them to be close to the amplifier inputs, not in the high-current zone near the shunt.
scope: RFH*/RFL*/CF* refs on 12vhpwr boards; owner IC derivable from shared net (RFH.2 net == INA240.IN+ net)
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'Kelvin pair 0.2-0.25mm tight matched pair over the In1 GND plane, sense off the INNER shunt edges, RC filter at the INA.' Placing the filter at the shunt end means the filter cap is embedded in the high-current pour zone, violating the thermal-separation constraint.
source: CLAUDE.md routing plan for 12VHPWR: 'RC filter at the INA'
check_method: For each (INA240 ref, RFH ref) pair linked by IN+ net, compute distance between RFH centroid and INA240.IN+ pad centroid; assert ≤ 3 mm.
existing_checker: derive_passive_spec in cec_synth_pipeline.py assigns RFH/RFL/CF to their INA240 owner

title: 12VHPWR sideband pins 13–16 must pass through J3→J4 and tap MCU GPIOs
rule: The 12V-2x6 sideband pins (J3/J4 pins 13–16: SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#) must be wired J3.13→J4.13, J3.14→J4.14, J3.15→J4.15, J3.16→J4.16 (pass-through for the GPU's own sense path) AND each must tap a dedicated ESP32-S3 GPIO (IO8/IO9/IO11/IO12) via a 1kΩ series resistor (R10–R13). No sideband pin may be left NC on either J3 or J4.
scope: J3/J4 pins 13–16 on 12vhpwr-standard; sideband nets SENSE0/SENSE1/CARD_PWR_STABLE/CARD_CBL_PRES#
rationale: §6.1 v3.4: 'the four 12V-2x6 sideband sense pins (13-16: SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#) now pass through J3->J4 AND each taps a free ESP32-S3 GPIO (IO8/9/11/12) via a 1k series R (R10-R13), so firmware can read the cable's advertised power capability + present/stable state'.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1 v3.4; CLAUDE.md: 'sideband sense pins (13-16) pass through J3->J4 AND tap GPIO IO8/9/11/12 via 1k R10-R13'
check_method: Netlist: for each sideband net, assert J3.pin_N and J4.pin_N both connected (pass-through). Assert each sideband net also connects to a 1kΩ resistor whose other end connects to the MCU GPIO. Count R10–R13 in BOM.

title: 12V-2x6 connector: pins 1–6 = +12V (inner row), pins 7–12 = GND (outer row) per CEM5.1
rule: On the 12VHPWR module's J3 and J4 Molex 219116 connectors: pins 1–6 must connect to the +12V rail; pins 7–12 must connect to GND. This follows PCIe CEM5.1 assignment. A swap would connect +12V to GND and destroy the GPU.
scope: J3 and J4 on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro; net names at each pin position in netlist
rationale: CLAUDE.md §2.8 LOCKED: 'pins 1-6 = +12V (the row ADJACENT to the signal pins), 7-12 = GND (the OUTER row)... VERIFY pins 7-12 = GND... since the schematic ties 7-12 to the GND plane (a swap shorts +12V to GND).' The connector is symmetric so polarity is a netlist assignment, not physically enforced.
source: CLAUDE.md §2.8: 'SAFETY: the connector is symmetric (both rows POWER); +12V vs GND is a system/CEM assignment — VERIFY pins 7-12 = GND'
check_method: Netlist: assert J3/J4 pins 1–6 connect to net containing '+12V' or 'SENSEP*_HI'. Assert pins 7–12 connect to net 'GND'. Assert pins 13–16 connect to sideband nets.

title: EPS/PCIe Mini-Fit Jr connector: GND on pins 1–4, +12V on pins 5–8
rule: On EPS and PCIe module J_IN*/J_OUT* Molex 87427/45586 connectors: pins 1–4 must connect to GND; pins 5–8 must connect to the +12V sense net (SENSEC*_HI/SENSEC*_LO). This is the correct EPS12V/EATX12V standard assignment. The inverted assignment (+12V on 1–4, GND on 5–8) was a known bug corrected in the schematic and gen-modules.py.
scope: All J_IN* and J_OUT* refs on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port
rationale: CLAUDE.md EPS pinout fix: 'The interposer's 4 Mini-Fit Jr connectors had +12V on pads 1-4 / GND on 5-8 -- the FLIPPED assignment vs the EPS12V/EATX12V standard. Corrected to GND on pads 1-4, +12V on pads 5-8.'
source: CLAUDE.md: 'EPS 8-pin power-connector pinout fix... Corrected to GND on pads 1-4, +12V on pads 5-8'
check_method: Netlist: for each J_IN*/J_OUT* ref, assert pins 1–4 net contains 'GND'; pins 5–8 net contains 'SENSEC' or '+12V'.

title: High-current F.Cu/B.Cu via stitching must be ≤ 5 mm pitch along the lane
rule: Along each high-current lane (J_IN→shunt→J_OUT corridor), via stitching connecting F.Cu to B.Cu pours must be placed at ≤ 5 mm pitch. This ensures the combined F+B cross-section carries the full current without relying on a single long trace on one layer.
scope: GND and *_HI net vias within the high-current corridor on EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'stitch F<->B ~5mm down each lane'. The electrothermal model accounts for parallel F+B cross-section; widely-spaced stitching leaves long single-layer segments that fail the temperature gate.
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR routing plan: 'stitch F<->B ~5mm down each lane'
check_method: For each high-current net lane, find vias sorted by position along the lane direction; assert max gap between consecutive vias ≤ 5 mm.

title: High-current 12V pours must be added AFTER Freerouting, not before
rule: In any automated routing flow using Freerouting (cec_fr), the high-current copper zone pours (add_power_pours / derive_power_pours) must be applied to the board AFTER the Freerouting SES import. Adding pours before running Freerouting is prohibited: doing so reshapes Freerouting's global routing solution and breaks the Kelvin gate by stranding sense traces on inner layers inside the pour boundary.
scope: Automated routing pipeline using cec_fr on any EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR board
rationale: CLAUDE.md Done: 'THE KEY INSIGHT was ORDERING: an earlier pass had concluded pour-THEN-route — WRONG... a pour on an already-routed net can only ADD copper, never strand the sense tap that shares the net node. Two attempts both regressed kelvin_ok.'
source: CLAUDE.md Done (route-to-clean + full agent pipeline): 'pour AFTER the route: FR routes everything first... THEN lay the 12V pours as ADDITIVE same-net copper'
check_method: Code review of cec_fr.import_ses() call sequence: assert add_power_pours() is called AFTER import_ses(), never before export_dsn(). In pipeline logs, assert POUR step timestamp > ROUTE step timestamp.
existing_checker: cec_fr.import_ses() wires power_pours param as a post-import step (verified in Done notes)

title: Rail voltage divider output must stay within ESP32 ADC input range at max rail voltage
rule: The 47kΩ/10kΩ rail voltage divider (R5/R6 on 12VHPWR-Standard; equivalent on other boards) must produce ≤ 3.2 V at the ADC pin under the maximum expected rail voltage (15 V on 12VHPWR, 14 V on 24-pin 12V rail). With the nominal 47k/10k ratio (attenuation factor 10/57 = 0.1754), Vout_max = 15 × 0.1754 = 2.63 V < 3.3 V ADC reference — within range. Any change to R5/R6 values must preserve this constraint.
scope: Rail divider network (R5, R6) and VRAIL_DIV net on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro, atx-24pin
rationale: ESP32 ADC maximum input is the reference voltage (3.3 V or REF3030 = 3.0 V on 12VHPWR-Standard). Exceeding it clamps the ADC or damages the input. The 47k/10k ratio is sized for margin below VDD under a 15 V maximum.
source: CLAUDE.md: '47k/10k rail-voltage divider into a 7th ADC channel (GPIO7)'; REF3030 = 3.0 V reference on 12VHPWR-Standard so ADC max is 3.0 V
check_method: BOM: assert R5 == 47kΩ and R6 == 10kΩ (ratio 4.7:1). Calculate Vout = Vrail_max × R6/(R5+R6); assert Vout ≤ 3.0 V (REF3030 boards) or ≤ 3.3 V (non-REF boards).

title: Rail voltage divider resistors must be 0.1% tolerance for REF3030 ratiometric accuracy
rule: On 12VHPWR-Standard, the rail divider resistors R5 (47kΩ) and R6 (10kΩ) must be 0.1% tolerance, ≤ 25 ppm/°C TCR. The REF3030 ratiometric reference cancels ADC gain/offset errors but NOT divider-ratio errors; a 1% resistor pair contributes ±1% voltage measurement error, degrading the target ±0.3–0.5% accuracy back to ±1%. Same requirement applies to the INA240 input filter resistors RFH*/RFL* (10 Ω, 0.1%, 50 ppm) for AC CMRR on transient capture.
scope: R5, R6 on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro; RFH*/RFL* on same boards
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'the REF3030 ratiometric ref does NOT cancel divider-ratio error, so 0.1% is required for the ~0.3-0.5% V channel. Repointed R5 -> Yageo RT0402BRD0747KL (C728561, 47k 0.1% 25ppm) and R6 -> RT0402BRD0710KL (C190095, 10k 0.1% 25ppm)'.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'tolerance fix: the rail divider R5/R6 carry Tolerance=0.1% (v3.8 spec) but had been mis-sourced to 1% UNI-ROYAL 0402WGF parts'
check_method: BOM Tolerance field for R5, R6: assert '0.1%'. MPN check: C728561 (47k) and C190095 (10k) are the locked parts. For RFH*/RFL*: assert MPN == C705642 (RT0402BRE0710RL, 10R 0.1%/50ppm).

title: INA240A3 must be the SOIC-8 D package (INA240A3DR), never the TSSOP PW package
rule: The INA240 current-sense amplifier must be ordered and placed as INA240A3DR (SOIC-8, D package, LCSC C2060584). The TSSOP/PW variant (INA240A3PW) has a completely different pin assignment and must not be used — it would connect V+/IN−/IN+/GND to wrong nets.
scope: All INA240 refs (U1–U6 on 12vhpwr-standard, U1–U6 on 12vhpwr-pro); Value field in BOM
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'the orderable MPN MUST be the D part (INA240A3DR), never the PW — the symbol value is currently package-ambiguous INA240A3 (pin the D suffix + LCSC# at the 12VHPWR BOM pass).' The SOIC-8 D pinout is verified against SBOS662C Fig 6-2.
source: CLAUDE.md: 'INA240 D/SOIC-8 confirmed vs datasheet Fig 6-2 AND our SOIC-8 footprint; the PW/TSSOP package has a DIFFERENT pinout'
check_method: BOM MPN field for INA240 refs: assert MPN contains 'INA240A3DR' (D suffix). LCSC: assert C2060584. Footprint: assert SOIC-8, not TSSOP.

title: INA228/238/240 count must match cable or pin count per board
rule: The number of primary sense ICs must equal the sensed channel count: EPS = 2 INA238; PCIe-2port = 2 INA238; PCIe-3port = 3 INA238; 12VHPWR-Standard = 6 INA240; 24-pin = 4 INA228 (one per rail: 12V, 5V, 3V3, 5VSB). Any deviation is a sensing gap.
scope: All INA* refs on every module board; count derivable from board name → expected count table in spec §6.1
rationale: §6.1 per-module sensing spec. A missing INA means a cable or pin has no current measurement, creating a hole in the telemetry data silently.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.1; CLAUDE.md board table
check_method: BOM count of INA228 refs on atx-24pin: assert == 4. INA238 on eps-8pin: == 2. INA238 on pcie-2port: == 2. INA238 on pcie-3port: == 3. INA240 on 12vhpwr-standard: == 6.
existing_checker: chk_kelvin_topology in cec_synth_pipeline.py (partial); CONFORMANCE chk_shunt_values implicitly requires correct count

title: Shunt count must equal sense IC count — one shunt per INA
rule: The number of shunt resistors RS* must equal the number of primary sense ICs (INA228/238/240) on each module board. Each sense IC must be in a one-to-one Kelvin-sense relationship with exactly one shunt. No IC may share a shunt with another IC (except INA181 which has its own sense path on the same shunt as the INA238).
scope: RS* refs and INA* refs on all module boards; bijection derivable from *_HI/*_LO net topology
rationale: §6.4 and §6.8. A shared shunt between two primary INA ICs would mean the sense terminals are shared, breaking the independent Kelvin measurement per channel and producing correlated errors.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4, §6.8
check_method: For each RS*, count distinct INA228/238/240 refs connected to its *_HI/*_LO nets via Kelvin pair; assert count == 1. Total RS* count must equal total INA228/238/240 count.

title: No copper path must bypass a shunt in the high-current force loop
rule: In the J_IN → shunt → J_OUT path, there must be no alternate low-resistance copper connection that allows current to flow from J_IN to J_OUT without passing through the shunt element. This includes: no direct via connecting the J_IN HI net to the J_OUT HI net outside the shunt body; no GND pour copper bridging the HI and LO shunt pads on the same side of the board.
scope: SENSEC*_HI / SENSEC*_LO net topology on EPS/PCIe; +12V / GND on 12VHPWR per-pin lanes
rationale: A bypass path creates a current divider around the shunt, causing the INA to underread the true cable current. This is the core interposer measurement integrity requirement.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.8; §6.4; implicit in the interposer topology
check_method: Netlist connectivity: assert that SENSEC*_HI and SENSEC*_LO nets share no copper connection except through the RS* footprint pads. Graph check: remove RS* from the netlist and assert SENSEC*_HI and SENSEC*_LO are disconnected.
existing_checker: cec_score.py kelvin_ok gate detects routing failures that result in stranded sense nodes

title: Shunt parts must be low-TCR precision metal-element resistors
rule: All RS* shunt resistors must be metal-element (metal strip, foil, or metal alloy) types with TCR ≤ 75 ppm/°C. Wire-wound, thick-film, or thin-film resistors with TCR > 75 ppm/°C are prohibited. The candidate part CSS2H-2512R-1L00F (LCSC C4175647, ±1%, 75 ppm) meets this requirement for EPS/PCIe.
scope: All RS* refs on all module boards; BOM Tolerance, TCR, and MPN fields
rationale: §6.4 LOCKED: 'Low-TCR precision metal-element shunts, four-wire Kelvin sense.' In a high-current environment (40–55 A), even 75 ppm/°C TCR produces a 0.375% reading shift at a 50°C temperature rise — the dominant accuracy term after Kelvin correction.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.4: 'Low-TCR precision metal-element shunts, four-wire Kelvin sense (§6.8)'
check_method: BOM: assert RS* MPN resolves to a metal-element datasheet (Bourns CSS2H, Vishay WSK, or equivalent). Flag any RS* with only a generic R_2512 value and no MPN (OQ-11 pending, but must be flagged before BOM freeze).

title: [OQ-10] EPS/PCIe ~40–55 A shunt vertical transition method is unresolved
rule: The vertical transition strategy for the ~40–55 A EPS/PCIe per-cable shunt sites (copper coin vs. filled-via field vs. plated slot) must NOT be assumed as via field until OQ-10 is resolved. Any automated placer or router must treat this as an advisory flag rather than assume a via-based solution. If a via-field approach is used (current default), the via count and sizing per via-field-sized-for-current constraint still applies.
scope: RS* shunt pads on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port vertical transitions between F.Cu and B.Cu
rationale: OQ-10 is explicitly open. A copper coin or plated slot would require a special fab process not reflected in the current gerber output. Silently assuming standard drill vias and then shipping to fab risks a board that cannot carry full current.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §6.7: 'For the ~40 to 55A EPS/PCIe per-cable class, a copper coin or inlay is the right tool'; CLAUDE.md OQ-10: 'Bundled-shunt vertical transition (copper coin vs filled-via field vs plated slot) — open'
check_method: Flag any EPS/PCIe board that has not documented a resolution for OQ-10 in its board spec or README. Automated check: if fab notes do not reference 'copper coin' or 'plated slot', emit advisory.

title: [OQ-11] EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR shunt part selection is not locked
rule: The specific shunt part MPN for EPS, PCIe, and 12VHPWR boards is not yet locked (OQ-11). The BOM must flag each RS* ref with a Note property indicating OQ-11 is open before any fab release. Do not treat CSS2H-2512R-1L00F as locked — it is a candidate only.
scope: All RS* refs on eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port, 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'RS1/RS2 the 0.5mΩ 2512 shunt (OQ-11 open)'; 'RS shunt OQ-11 still open (CSS2H-2512R-1L00F candidate, +/-1%/75ppm)'. Shipping a fab without resolving OQ-11 risks a tolerance or TCR mismatch.
source: CLAUDE.md OQ-11: 'Per-module shunt part selection (value, TCR, tolerance, package, power) per the §6.4 shunt table — open'
check_method: BOM: assert RS* Note field contains 'OQ-11' for EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR boards. Block fab release if OQ-11 is unflagged.

title: ESP32 antenna keepout must be honoured on Hub (wireless); may be dropped on wired-only modules
rule: On Hub boards (esp32-s3-wroom-1-n16r8): the ESP32 PCB antenna keepout zone (no copper under or adjacent to the antenna region per Espressif guidelines) must be honoured. On wired-only module boards (EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR-Standard — no RF): the ESP32 antenna keepout MAY be dropped to reclaim board area, enabling GND fill under the module body.
scope: U1 (ESP32) footprint on all boards; antenna keepout polygon in ESP32 footprint; Hub boards must honour it; module boards may drop it after explicit decision
rationale: CLAUDE.md: 'antenna keepout (respect_antenna_keepout -> the placer trims the ESP32 courtyard 219->153mm² via cec_pcb drop_keepout)... AND EMC's RF arm only fires if the radio is populated'. EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR modules are wire-only (RJ-45 + USB); disabling Wi-Fi/BT by firmware and dropping the keepout yields ~66mm² board area reduction per cec_pcb.drop_keepout().
source: CLAUDE.md: 'ESP32-C6 antenna keepout DROPPED (no wireless, per user) -> GND fills under it, courtyard trimmed to body'
check_method: For Hub boards: assert no copper zone fill intersects the ESP32 antenna keepout polygon. For module boards with no_antenna decision: assert board config records the keepout-drop explicitly (Stage-1 ask answered wired-only).

title: M3 mounting holes must be connected to GND (chassis ground bond)
rule: All M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via refs) on every module board must have their copper pad connected to the GND net and include at least 2 stitching vias to the inner GND plane. Isolated mounting holes floating at an undefined potential create ESD ingress paths from the metal chassis.
scope: All MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via refs on every board; derivable from footprint name pattern
rationale: CLAUDE.md: '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting' (Hub Standard). build_board() sets gnd_all=True for mounts. Ungrounded mounts are a common source of chassis-borne ESD reaching the board.
source: CLAUDE.md: '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting'; cec_pcb.build_board() gnd_all=True for mounts
check_method: Netlist: for each MountingHole* ref, assert its copper pad net == GND. PCB: assert ≥ 2 vias within 1.5 mm of pad centre on GND net.
existing_checker: build_board() in cec_pcb.py sets mount pads to GND net

title: 12VHPWR J4 output captive pigtail must have mechanical strain relief
rule: The J4 (load-side) captive soldered output pigtail on 12VHPWR modules must include strain-relief provisions: either a through-board cable clamp, a zip-tie anchor footprint (MountingHole or SlotHole near J4), or a potted/adhesive-fixed entry point. A bare soldered pigtail with no strain relief will fatigue and fracture the solder joints under cable routing stress.
scope: J4 pigtail exit on 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro; identifiable by the J4 Molex 219116 ref at the board bottom edge
rationale: CLAUDE.md §2.8: 'a captive soldered OUTPUT pigtail to the GPU (a 12V-2x6 cable soldered to the board, no detachable bridging cable) — the minimal-mated-pair form.' Without strain relief, thermal cycling and mechanical flexure on the GPU connection will eventually crack the J4 solder joints.
source: CLAUDE.md §2.8 LOCKED: 'board-mount right-angle MALE header IN (PSU cable plugs in) + a captive soldered OUTPUT pigtail to the GPU'
check_method: Check .kicad_pcb for a MountingHole or SlotHole within 10 mm of J4 centroid on the bottom board edge intended for strain relief. Flag if absent.
